description: Return the largest number of real posts assigned in a popular matching for a bounded one-sided market with tied applicant preferences.

source.title: Popular Matchings
source.reuse: Mathematical algorithm descriptions only; the author-hosted paper states personal-use permission and is not redistributed. Contract, fixtures, oracles, and ports are clean-room.

input.ranking_rules: Every applicant has a nonempty list. IDs are zero based; each applicant-post pair occurs once; ranks are in 1..P, contiguous per applicant, and equal ranks encode ties. At least one applicant rank group contains two or more posts so every valid frame exercises tied preferences.
input.last_resorts: Applicant a has private post P+a, ranked below all listed posts; it makes matchings applicant-complete and is excluded from the result.

output.meaning: Maximum number of real posts assigned in any popular applicant-complete matching; zero means no popular matching exists.
output.maximum_result_derivation: At most min(A,P) real posts can be assigned, and both counts are at most four. A popular matching must contain a maximum matching on the nonempty rank-one graph, so zero denotes nonexistence.

algorithm_profile.primary: Build the rank-one graph and a deterministic maximum matching; classify vertices E/O/U by an alternating forest rooted at every exposed applicant and post, with private last resorts isolated and even. Keep rank-one edges and each applicant's top-ranked even posts, then delete O-O and O-U edges. Augment the rank-one matching in this filtered graph to an applicant-complete popular matching. In a second phase delete all private last-resort edges and augment to maximize real-post use while retaining maximum rank-one cardinality; finally restore last-resort edges and augment to applicant completeness.
algorithm_profile.independent: Enumerate all applicant-complete assignments over listed posts and private last resorts. For each candidate, compare it against every other assignment by the direct applicant vote definition; retain the largest real-post count among candidates that never lose a vote comparison.
algorithm_profile.tie_policy: Applicants, posts, augmenting roots, and adjacency scans use ascending IDs. Alternating-forest roots are enqueued as unmatched applicants, unmatched real posts, then private last resorts. A matching phase repeats ascending applicant passes with single-path DFS augmentation until no augmentation succeeds; this bounded implementation does not use Hopcroft-Karp batching.

complexity.primary_time: O(A*(A+P)*(E+A)) with fixed A,P<=4 and E<=16, including repeated augmenting passes

workspace.meaning: Fixed rank matrix, rank-one matching, alternating classes, reduced graph, matching-phase state, and bounded vote-enumeration reference state.
